The two query services independently materialize all Posted treasury movements and calculate each account balance as destination amount minus source amount. The filter and projection are semantically equivalent for each configured account, including transfers (debit source, credit destination). The Daily Statement separately exposes day-filtered movement rows; that is a different period-scoped detail view, not an inconsistency with its explicitly all-time current balance. Existing tests assert dashboard balance independence from selected reporting period and day filtering of displayed movement rows, but do not compare dashboard and daily-statement TreasuryNow values under transfers/non-posted rows. No current defect found; duplicated financial formula is a drift risk.

The owner dashboard sums positive QuantityMilliUnits without Direction, while the inventory overview/domain balances sign Out as negative. Runtime/database verification remains unexecuted.

Record as a conditional documentation/contract gap, not a confirmed financial defect.

semantic_groups.decision: SOURCE-CONFIRMED REPORT-CONSISTENCY DIVERGENCE FOR A REVERSED MULTI-DATE REQUEST: the endpoint accepts the constructed reversed BusinessDateRange; the headline query normalizes UTC endpoints by swapping them and reads the corresponding dates, while daily-series point enumeration uses the unnormalized From/To and returns no points. Policy on reject-versus-normalize is not specified. Cross-reference existing FIN-CAND-REPORT-RANGE-001; no new canonical finding ID.

NO DIVERGENCE IN THE REVIEWED QUERY PATH: the cashier sends the current session user ID; the server middleware resolves bearer identity and rejects a mismatching actorUserId before the endpoint runs; the endpoint then checks orders_view_all and otherwise limits results to the currently open shift. The client performs only local search over the returned authorized collection. The server route also loads user by the query ID, but the pipeline guard binds that ID to the bearer actor for this route. No separate finding is created. This does not clear SEC-001 JSON-body casing behavior or other routes.

semantic_groups.decision: SOURCE-CONFIRMED SEMANTIC DIVERGENCE; same canonical defect FIN-013, no new finding. LoadStockAsync sums QuantityMilliUnits for every movement without applying Direction. InventoryRules.StockBalanceMilliUnits and InventoryQueryService.GetInventoryOverviewAsync add In and subtract Out. RecordWasteHandler stores positive quantity with Direction=Out. Example: 10,000 In + 2,000 Out produces 12,000 on dashboard versus 8,000 in inventory overview; an existing integration test asserts the 8,000 inventory balance. Dashboard may therefore suppress a low-stock warning.

No client/server rule-validation divergence or stale-rule charging defect was confirmed in the reviewed path. Cashier preflight constrains ordinary input; server/domain independently enforce nonblank name, nonempty known product set, positive fixed price, valid weekday range and offers_manage authorization. Checkout does not trust client amounts and revalidates requested rule against current server rule/product/time; invalid/stale rule falls back to list price, then freezes resolved price/rule metadata. No new finding. Existing source documents intentional midnight wrapping, one-sided time restriction ignored, and overlapping offers allowed; do not infer different policy.

Both WinUI clients submit the selected service fee and ID/name consistently, but checkout binds neither fee to the configured active service in server source. This is supplemental evidence for FIN-016, not a duplicate finding; owner must decide authoritative fee versus authorized override. No runtime executed.

The client rejects nonpositive amounts and values above its displayed remaining refundable balance, while the server independently clamps any requested amount to the remaining amount and rejects a resulting zero. This is a deliberate permissive server boundary rather than an over-refund path: order locking, aggregate invariants, protected source-account balance, transaction, immutable refund record and treasury movement constrain effects. Existing tests explicitly cover server clamp, same-key replay and concurrent distinct refunds without aggregate overdraw. No new divergence or finding was confirmed. Tests were read, not run.

PreviewCloseBlockersAsync, CloseBusinessDayHandler and OwnerDashboardQueryService all call BusinessDayCloseEvaluator.EvaluateAsync. The GET and close routes bind to those consumers; the existing integration test opens a shift, checks OPEN_SHIFT in preview, attempts close, and asserts identical blocker-code sets. This is shared logic, not independently duplicated blocker rules; no divergence or new finding confirmed. Evaluator inputs include global outstanding shifts/custodies/journal entries/pending electronic payments and global protected balances, while checklist and some discrepancy checks are business-day scoped. Global-vs-day closure policy needs explicit owner/system scope confirmation, but source alone does not establish a defect; deployment topology may intentionally allow only one active day.
